cards.text: It's just before the Passover Feast. Jesus knows His hour has come to leave this world and return to the Father. And He has loved His own who were in the world.

cards.question: Jesus has loved His own who were in the world. How far does that love go?

cards.text: The evening meal is underway. But there's a dark detail about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot: the devil has already put something into his heart.

cards.question: What has the devil put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot?

cards.text: Now here's what Jesus knows. The Father has delivered all things into His hands, and He came from God and is returning to God.

cards.question: Jesus knows all things are in His hands. True or false: He stays seated at the supper.

cards.text: He gets up from the supper, lays aside His outer garments, and wraps a towel around His waist. If somebody handed ME all things, friend, I'd call a press conference, and HE grabs a towel.

cards.question: Jesus pours water into a basin and begins to wash the disciples' ___.

cards.text: He dries them with the towel that's around Him. Then He comes to Simon Peter, one of His disciples, who asks, "Lord, are You going to wash my feet?"

cards.question: Jesus replies to Peter. True or false: Jesus tells Peter he will never understand what He is doing.

cards.text: Peter's answer: "Never shall You wash my feet!" That's me when a baker offers to scrub my mixing bowls: NO, no, no, I've GOT it.

cards.question: Jesus answers Peter. Unless Jesus washes him, what does Jesus say happens?

answers.text: Peter has no part with Him
Peter has to leave the room

cards.question: Now Peter wants more. He asks Jesus to wash not only his feet, but his ___ and his ___ as well.

cards.text: From NEVER to EVERYTHING in one breath. That's me with the snooze button, friend: dead asleep, then SPRINTING for the oven.
Jesus tells Peter that whoever has already bathed needs only to wash his feet, and he will be completely clean.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells the disciples that every one of them is clean.
Jesus says not all of them are clean, because He knew who would ___ Him.

cards.text: When He's finished washing their feet, Jesus puts His outer garments back on and reclines with them again. Then He asks, "Do you know what I have done for you?"

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells the disciples they're right to call Him Teacher and Lord.
Their Lord and Teacher just washed their feet. So what does Jesus say the disciples should do?

answers.text: Never let Him do it again

cards.text: Jesus says He has set them an example, so they should do as He has done for them. He didn't hand them a pamphlet on serving, friend; He handed them clean feet.
Jesus opens with "Truly, truly," and when He says it twice, I lean in. Then He tells them who is greater than whom.

cards.question: Jesus says no ___ is greater than his master, nor is a ___ greater than the one who sent him.
True or false: Jesus says the disciples will be blessed just for knowing these things.

cards.text: Blessed if they DO them. I can read a cookie recipe all day long, friend, and not one cookie has ever baked itself.
Then Jesus says He isn't speaking about all of them. He knows whom He has chosen.

cards.question: Jesus quotes Scripture about someone who "has lifted up his heel against Me." Who does it say that is?
Jesus is telling them all this before it happens, so that when it comes to pass, they will ___ that He is He.

cards.text: One more "Truly, truly." Jesus says whoever receives the one He sends receives Him.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever receives the one He sends receives Him. And whoever receives Jesus receives whom?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Supper's still going, and trust me, this night is not done.

findings.problem: Judas appears here for the first time, but the card never says who he is. It gives only his father's name, "the son of Simon Iscariot," and never says he is one of Jesus' disciples.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to guess Peter's exact wording. No earlier card points to "hands" and "head" over "back" or "eyes," so the pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong word "clothes" isn't a body part. The right answers and the other wrong answers are all body parts, so "clothes" is easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card tells no new part of the passage. It only reacts to John 13:9, which card 13 already covered. A joke is carrying the whole card instead of riding along on a moment of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The core action is Peter flipping from refusing Jesus' washing to asking for more. The snooze-button comparison shows someone going from asleep to rushing, which is a different action. "In one breath" also adds a timing the text doesn't give.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus tells "the disciples." The text says "Jesus told him," meaning Peter (John 13:10). The card names an audience the text doesn't name.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card tells no new part of the passage. It only reacts to John 13:17, which card 7 already covered. The card is only a joke.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This is a who question, but the wrong answers, "A stranger in the crowd" and "A soldier at the gate," are made-up generic people, not real details from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
